Earnings Call Transcript
V2X (VVX) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

May 4, 2026 at 5:39PM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


DATE
Monday, May 4, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
President & Chief Executive Officer — Jeremy C. Wensinger
Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer — Shawn M. Mural
Vice President, Treasury, Investor Relations, & Corporate Development — Michael J. Smith
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
TAKEAWAYS
Revenue
-- $1.254 billion, representing a 23% increase year over year driven by organic growth across training, foreign military sales, prototyping, and engineering programs.
Adjusted Net Income
-- $48.1 million, up 53%, reflecting contributions from volume and mix, and improved operational execution.
Adjusted EBITDA
-- $85.6 million, increasing 28% with a margin of 6.8%, a 20-basis-point improvement year over year.
Adjusted Diluted EPS
-- $1.53, an increase of 55% from the prior year.
Bookings
-- $4.1 billion in new awards for the quarter, resulting in a record quarterly book-to-bill ratio of 3.2x and a trailing twelve months ratio of 1.5x.
Total Backlog
-- $13.8 billion, up from $11.1 billion at year-end, providing increased revenue visibility.
Contract Mix
-- Approximately $3.3 billion of bookings driven by the T-6 award, with backlog generally converting over five to seven years, and T-6 extending to ten years.
Customer Diversification
-- 21% of revenue from customers outside of the U.S. Army, Navy, and Air Force, increased from 13% a year ago.
Liquidity
-- $200 million in cash and a $500 million revolver with zero drawn, supporting ongoing investments and capital deployment.
Adjusted Operating Cash Flow
-- ($22.1 million) use during the quarter, with management stating improved cadence and expectations for more favorable performance through the year.
Raised 2026 Guidance
-- Management provided increased guidance: revenue of $4.825 billion to $4.975 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $345 million to $360 million, adjusted diluted EPS of $5.75 to $6.15, and adjusted net cash from operations of $160 million to $180 million.
Segment Performance
-- U.S. business revenue rose 40% year over year to over $800 million, supported by national security and modernization activities.
Geographic Positioning
-- Management stated strong and stable market posture in both Europe and the Middle East, with $500 million in Kuwait backlog and expectations of continued execution in both regions.
T-6 Program Outlook
-- Annual revenue from T-6 now expected to reach $175 million to $180 million, exceeding previous guidance.
SG&A Expenses
-- $12 million in nonrecurring professional fees incurred in the quarter, with a smaller portion expected in the second quarter.
Artificial Intelligence Initiatives
-- Management introduced three enterprise AI platforms internally, reported accelerated adoption and cost-efficiency gains, and highlighted prototype deployment in aerospace sustainment with Google, Tactile, and NVIDIA.
Visibility
-- Under contract, revenue visibility increased to 94% for full-year 2026, up from a previously disclosed 85%.
Contract Structure
-- Ongoing time and materials work for national security customers contributed $70 million to $80 million to guidance increases; management expects this work to continue through the year.
Bid Velocity
-- On track for a 30% year-over-year increase in bid volume, supporting expansion of future backlog.
SUMMARY
Management delivered record-high bookings and backlog, achieving significant revenue, profit, and margin growth for the quarter, while raising full-year 2026 financial guidance on the strength of contract wins and robust market demand. The T-6 program contributed $3.3 billion to quarterly bookings and is now expected to reach $175 million to $180 million in annual revenue, compared to previous estimates of $140 million to $160 million. Management confirmed 94% revenue visibility for the year, noted improved operational cash flow cadence, and highlighted ongoing investments in artificial intelligence that are delivering measurable internal efficiencies and forming core components of new customer-facing solutions.
Chief Financial Officer Mural said, "Of the $150 million raise at the midpoint, about $70 million to $80 million is associated with this activity," identifying clear drivers of updated guidance.
Management stated that startup phases of multiple recent awards, especially in aerospace and modernization sustainment, mean that long-term margin expansion "mature over time," with further guidance planned later in the year.
The T-6 award, comprising approximately one-quarter of total backlog, drives the average contract duration beyond historical norms, with most backlog still expected to convert within five to seven years.
Adjusted operating cash flow in the quarter was a net outflow of $22.1 million, but management expects full-year operating cash flow to be solid, supported by an undrawn $500 million credit facility.
Management indicated that approximately 21% of quarterly revenue was from customers outside the three largest U.S. military branches, underscoring continued exposure to diversified end markets.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
Book-to-Bill Ratio
: A measure comparing the dollar value of incoming orders to revenue recognized during a period; indicates the pace of backlog growth.
Trailing Twelve Months (TTM)
: The cumulative metric over the most recent twelve-month period, useful for smoothing quarterly fluctuations.
Operational Tempo (Ops Tempo)
: The rate of activity or deployment for military support contracts, affecting both revenue and resource requirements.
Initial Operating Capability (IOC)
: The first phase when a program or asset becomes operational and provides limited deployment or use.
Time and Materials (T&M) Contract
: A contract structure in which payments are based on actual labor hours and material costs, often used for programs with evolving requirements.
